author: statistical
note: bars[0] is the reference (most recently closed) bar; index increases going back in time. Bars are [open,high,low,close,tick_volume]. default_filler_series is a flat range-1.0 close-100 bar used to pad long windows without creating a pattern.

fixtures.rationale: Mean reversion setup means the last close is stretched far from its recent average. Close 105 sits 4.75 above the 20-bar SMA 100.25 while 2xATR is only 2.42, so price is over-extended and primed to snap back.
Not stretched: close 100.5 is essentially on the 20-bar average (deviation 0.475 vs 2xATR 2.01). Price hugging its mean is the opposite of an over-extended, revert-ready state.

Price drifted down to close 99 (deviation 0.95) but that is well within normal wobble: 2xATR is 2.02. A modest move that does not clear two ATRs is not an extreme worth fading (attacks the magnitude clause on the downside).
Dead-flat market: every bar open=high=low=close=100 so ATR is 0 and there is no dispersion to be extended from. With no volatility there can be no over-extension (attacks the atr>0 guard).
Just INSIDE the 2xATR line: close 102.6 gives deviation |102.6-100.13|=2.47, above 2xATR=2.17 (ATR=(2.7+19)/20=1.085). Deviation exceeds the two-ATR threshold by ~14%, so the setup fires.
Just OUTSIDE (below) the 2xATR line: close 101.9 gives deviation |101.9-100.095|=1.805, under 2xATR=2.10 (ATR=(2.0+19)/20=1.05). Falls ~14% short of the two-ATR threshold, so no setup.

Z-score high means the close is many standard deviations above the 20-bar mean. Close 105 against a series otherwise pinned at 100 gives z=+4.36 (the single-outlier maximum sqrt(19)), a textbook statistical extreme to the upside.
Wrong sign: close 95 sits far BELOW the mean (z=-4.36). A high z-score requires being above the mean, so a deep negative z must not register (attacks the direction of the >2.5 test).

Close 103 is above the mean but the series is itself noisy (background +/-2.0), giving sd~2.01 and z=+1.42. A move of one-and-a-half sigma is ordinary variation, not a statistical extreme (attacks the magnitude relative to dispersion).
Every close equals 100 so the standard deviation is 0 and a z-score is undefined. With no dispersion nothing can be an outlier (attacks the sd>0 guard).
Just INSIDE the z>2.5 line: background +/-0.85, close 103 yields sd=1.038 and z=+2.745, roughly 10% ABOVE the 2.5 cutoff, so it fires.
Just OUTSIDE the z>2.5 line: background +/-1.15, close 103 yields sd=1.272 and z=+2.241, roughly 10% BELOW the 2.5 cutoff, so it does not fire.

Z-score low means the close is many standard deviations below the 20-bar mean. Close 95 against a series pinned at 100 gives z=-4.36 (single-outlier minimum -sqrt(19)), a textbook statistical extreme to the downside.
Wrong sign: close 105 sits far ABOVE the mean (z=+4.36). A low z-score requires being below the mean, so a large positive z must not register (attacks the direction of the <-2.5 test).
Close 97 is below the mean but against a noisy background (+/-2.0, sd~2.01) z=-1.42. One-and-a-half sigma down is normal variation, not an extreme (attacks magnitude relative to dispersion).
Every close equals 100 so standard deviation is 0 and a z-score is undefined; nothing can be an outlier with zero dispersion (attacks the sd>0 guard).
Just INSIDE the z<-2.5 line: background +/-0.85, close 97 yields sd=1.038 and z=-2.745, roughly 10% BEYOND (more negative than) the -2.5 cutoff, so it fires.
Just OUTSIDE the z<-2.5 line: background +/-1.15, close 97 yields sd=1.272 and z=-2.241, roughly 10% SHORT OF (less negative than) the -2.5 cutoff, so it does not fire.
High volatility percentile means today's range dwarfs the recent norm. Bar range 5.0 against 100 prior bars all of range 1.0: all 100 are below it (pct=1.00), the widest bar in the window.
Bar range 0.5 against 100 prior bars of range 1.0: zero are below it (pct=0.00). A contracted bar is at the BOTTOM of the volatility distribution, the opposite of a high-percentile bar.
Bar range 1.0 sits in the middle of a split history (50 bars at 0.5, 50 at 3.0): only the 50 narrow bars are below it (pct=0.50). A median-volatility bar is not a high-percentile extreme.
Just INSIDE the 90th-percentile line: history has 93 bars of range 1.0 and 7 of range 3.0; bar range 2.0 is above exactly 93 of them, pct=0.93 which clears the >=0.90 cutoff.
Just OUTSIDE the 90th-percentile line: history has 87 bars of range 1.0 and 13 of range 3.0; bar range 2.0 is above only 87, pct=0.87 which is below the 0.90 cutoff.
Low volatility percentile means today's range is among the narrowest recently. Bar range 0.2 against 100 prior bars all of range 1.0: none are below it (pct=0.00), the tightest bar in the window.
Bar range 5.0 against 100 prior bars of range 1.0: all 100 are below it (pct=1.00). A wide bar is at the TOP of the volatility distribution, the opposite of a low-percentile bar.
Bar range 1.0 in a split history (50 bars at 0.5, 50 at 3.0): the 50 narrow bars are below it (pct=0.50). A median-volatility bar is not a low-percentile extreme.
Just INSIDE the 10th-percentile line: history has 7 bars of range 0.5 and 93 of range 3.0; bar range 1.0 is above only 7 of them, pct=0.07 which is under the <=0.10 cutoff.
Just OUTSIDE the 10th-percentile line: history has 13 bars of range 0.5 and 87 of range 3.0; bar range 1.0 is above 13 of them, pct=0.13 which is over the 0.10 cutoff.

A fractal breakout is a local swing high (bar 2 high 105 above its neighbours bars 1/3/4 at 103/102/101) that the current bar then closes ABOVE (close 105.5). The repaired predicate detects this as a breakout; bar 0 printing a higher high (106) no longer voids it.
Bar 2 is not a swing high: bar 3 high 106 towers over bar 2 high 104, so there is no fractal to break out from. No pattern, expected false (code agrees).

A clean fractal peak exists at bar 2 (high 105 above bars 1/3/4) but the current bar closes at 102.5, well BELOW the peak. Fractal without a breakout close is not the pattern; expected false (code agrees).
The immediate right neighbour bar 1 (high 106) exceeds bar 2 (high 105), so bar 2 is not a local peak surrounded by lower bars. Not a fractal; expected false (code agrees).

Just INSIDE the breakout line: fractal peak bar 2 high 105.0, current bar closes 105.3, ABOVE the peak -> a breakout (true). The repaired predicate returns true even though bar 0 prints a higher high (105.5).
Just OUTSIDE the breakout line: same fractal peak bar 2 high 105.0, but current bar closes 104.7, BELOW the peak -> no breakout (false). The repaired predicate agrees on this side.
